analysis:
This batch contains only documentation changes: CHANGELOG.md (head lines 2359-3110 are older release history, with the new v0.10.2 candidate section at the top of the file outside the visible units) and removal of five changelog.d fragments (balanced-checkpoints-glm-super, desktop-release-pipeline, glm-bf16-ssd-checkpoints, glm-capture-under-load, glm-decoder-protection, glm-hidden-reasoning). No executable source, key handling, authorization or crypto code is changed here, so no direct regression is visible.

Security-relevant context from the removed fragments, all in the T-041 prefix-cache area and A-001:
- Balanced 4-bit SSD checkpoints for Nemotron Super and GLM use new cache namespaces (layout IDs). Old exact files miss once and age out via the TTL sweep, so the at-rest posture is unchanged in kind: same HMAC names, DBK3 encryption, TTL and KEK purge. Note the head excerpt says outputs are no longer bit-identical to uncached; this is a correctness/quality caveat, not a disclosure issue.
- GLM checkpoints now land on any 256-token boundary and capture under load. This slightly widens how much prefix material is cached and the TTFT oracle granularity (SEC-035, already accepted). Same-account scoping via coordinator-authored cacheSalt is not shown changing.
- The rollout note gates prefix caching on a coordinator allowlist tuple (model_id, aggregate sha, prompt_contract_id), which is consistent with the threat model's scope derivation.
- Removing the desktop release pipeline fragment only affects release notes; whether release-desktop.yml itself changed is outside the supplied evidence.
- GLM hidden reasoning (reasoning.exclude) withholds reasoning from the response but bills it; no leak evident.

Remaining questions for integration: the actual source changes behind these notes (KVCacheSSD, the checkpoint codec, and cache_route_keys.go) are not in this batch and should be examined by the passes covering them. In particular, confirm that the T-041 detection_hint items (AAD fields, HMAC tag derivation, TTL) are unchanged and that the finer 256-token checkpoint boundaries do not alter metadata. The threat model T-041 text may need a sentence about balanced 4-bit checkpoints and new layout namespaces.
